sentences.text: Procariama stood about 70 cm tall and weighed approximately 10 kg.
This bird had a more robust build than Psilopterus, characterized by comparatively shorter thigh bones.
The hypotarsus of Procariama's tarsometatarsus features two protrusions, one lateral and one medial, near the proximal end.
The genus name Procariama means "before Cariama", referring to the red-legged seriema, its closest living relative.
Specimen FM-P 14525 is an exquisitely preserved and nearly complete skeleton of Procariama.
The genus Procariama was first described by Cayetano Rovereto in 1914.
Three additional specimens of Procariama are known besides the lectotype.
Procariama belongs to the order Cariamiformes, whose only modern representatives are seriemas.
Procariama is classified within the family Phorusrhacidae.
In 2024, Procariama was reclassified as a member of the subfamily Psilopterinae.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Procariama as Mesembriornithinae.
Procariama lived in Argentina between 11 and 2 million years ago during the Late Miocene and Late Pliocene.
The Paleobi Database records the time range of Procariama as the Tortonian to Zanclean stages (8 to 3.8 million years ago).
Fossils of Procariama have been found in the Cerro Azul and Andalhuala Formations.
Fossils were found in the Andagalá and northern Belén departments of Catamarca province, and one site in La Pampa province.
